title: Anyone has a bunch of unfinished projects waiting for when AI gets even better?
author: FutureLynx_
selftext:
If we analyze the evolution of AI from 3 years ago to now. It's now 100 times more efficient.

So i imagine like in 2030 its probably going to make what is taking now weeks to finish in just a couple of hours.

I have a bunch of unfinished projects that I'm deliberately not touching.

If i finished them back then it would have been a waste of time, considering that AI can now help me finish them in much less time.

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body:
I am only working on one projects, but I am scheduling my tasks with AI progression in mind. As ab example, fleshing out the graphics early isnt optimal if AI modelling make great leaps soon, so I am doing simple graphics first.

The core game mechanics and level design will be less affected, so I am focusing on those first (which would probably be the right order even without AI).

comments.author: necronomicoder
comments.body:
Yes.  I have three game prototypes.  They aren't unfinished as much as i'm slowly iterating.  I improve the game and experiment with the gameplay on a regular basis but not working through the night on them.  When a new frontier model comes out I'll get them to evaluate and re-implement based on the spec and design notes/mistakes I documented.

  
Of the three games, one i'm happy with but needs more work on the core game-play.  I'd spend a few bucks on it, but I want it to be way more fun i.e. 10s of bucks.  The other was for my wife and is a bit more traditional (adventure/rpg/simulator), but I think i'll integrate it into a website as a rewards/social aspect, the last was to see how Astra compares to Fable (preview: they ran out of credits) on a 3d shooter that combines what I really like: punchy guns, gore, a tense gameplay loop etc.

  
I've got lots of other projects non-game related, but the games work best with experimenting on core gameplay and then committing when that's polished.

I love when people share their creations, prompts and techniques, really helps me think how to better get more out of the current models.

comments.author: yarrowy
comments.body: You could have seen earning money 3 years ago

comments.author: WhyWouldYou1111111
comments.body: Live this hot take lol I just upgraded some projects from ~ 2019 with AI over the past few weeks and it's hilarious how trivial it made it.

comments.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
comments.body: I have thought about that but it also seems like a bad idea. Games are art and you are the artist.  I’m not sure it’s a good idea to wait until technology catches up to how you want it to be just to finish art. Maybe finish your smaller projects first and keep your more ambitious ones for later?

replies.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
replies.body: Some of us are craftsmen and not artists.

comments.body: I have unfished prototypes that are being able to be finished. Making huge progress with opus 5 and sol 5.6. Dont have access to Astra. But all the assets were done by me.

comments.author: EQLMonk
comments.body:
I'm waiting until I can have ai turn my doodles into weight painted and rigged models that will maintain my art style and I can have it either do or rough out basic animations.

I've done it all by hand it's just a huge PITA.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: As I learned what AI could do, I'd abandon side projects I was doing back in Sonnet with Claude. I wasn't intentionally waiting, but recently pointed Fable 5.1 and it just....   when from stuck to "oh yea that's exactly what I wanted!"

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body: I make a model or animation and several assets whenever the idea pops into my head, so I have lots of cars and sheets and models that just go to nothing but might one day.
